name: TX-14
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Randy Weber seeking reelection with large financial edge
Democratic challenger minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price Weber near certain to win
model.rationale: Weber holds a decisive structural advantage in an R+12 district, has raised over $1 million against Bartie's $37,000, and faces no outside spending against him. Markets price his win at roughly 96%, and no polls or expert ratings suggest vulnerability.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Weber would be the first sign of trouble, but nothing currently indicates a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber is seeking another term in a southeast Texas district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan lean of about twelve points toward the GOP. He enters the general election with a well-funded campaign, roughly $900,000 on hand, and no organized outside opposition. Thurman Bartie, the Democratic nominee, has raised only about $37,000 and had just over $5,000 in cash as of the latest filings, leaving him little capacity to communicate with voters.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, and prediction markets give Weber roughly a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals point the same direction: incumbency, a large money advantage, and a favorable district all favor the Republican. The race is rated Safe R, with the main uncertainty being turnout patterns rather than a genuine competitive threat.
